About.title: About StockLens
About.what: StockLens is a free learning tool made for the PMF Investment Society. It helps you read the key numbers of a listed company and form your own opinion.
About.advice: Everything here is educational. StockLens is not a broker, you cannot buy or sell anything, and nothing on this site tells you what to do with your money. Analyst opinions are arguments to evaluate, not instructions.
About.data: Prices and company figures come from Yahoo Finance through an unofficial channel. They can be delayed (the delay is shown next to each price), incomplete or wrong. When a figure is missing we say so instead of guessing.
About.storage: No account, no ads, no tracking. This draft page will be completed with the full privacy and terms text before launch.
About.draft: Charts are drawn with TradingView Lightweight Charts, used under its licence.

explain.rule: Rule of thumb (a guide, not a law)

eps.title: Earnings per share (EPS)
eps.meaning: Profit for each share, last quarter, compared with what analysts expected.
eps.definition: The profit the company made, divided among all its shares. Also called BPA in French.
eps.rule: Beating or missing by a few percent is common. Look at several quarters, not just one.

pe.title: P/E ratio
pe.meaning: Years of profit it would take to earn back the price of one share.
pe.definition: How many times the yearly profit per share the market pays for one share. Read it as the number of years of profit needed to earn your money back.
pe.rule: A high P/E often means investors expect strong growth, a low one can mean low expectations or doubts. Compare with similar companies.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.meaning: The money the company earned by selling its products or services.
revenue.definition: Everything customers paid the company during the period, before any cost is removed. Also called sales.
revenue.formula: Price of each sale × number of sales
revenue.rule: Growing revenue is only good news if profit follows. Compare with the same period last year.

operating.title: Operating profit
operating.meaning: What is left after the costs of running the business, before interest and tax.
operating.definition: The profit from the company's everyday activity.
operating.formula: Revenue − operating costs. The margin is operating profit ÷ revenue.
operating.rule: Margins differ a lot between industries. Compare a company with its competitors.

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.meaning: The cash left after paying to run and maintain the business.
fcf.definition: Cash that came in, minus cash that went out to run the company and to buy equipment. It is what the company is really free to use.
fcf.formula: Cash from operations − investment in equipment and buildings
fcf.rule: A company can show a profit but little free cash flow, for example when it invests heavily. Look at both.

marketCap.title: Market capitalisation
marketCap.meaning: What the stock market says the whole company is worth today.
marketCap.definition: The price of one share multiplied by the number of shares. It is the price of the whole company, not the profit.
marketCap.rule: Companies above roughly 10 billion are often called large caps. Smaller companies tend to move more.
